subject: Proof of Deletion & Data Provenance for DSR - Acme Health
messages:
From: Jenny Alvarez <privacy@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proof of Deletion & Data Provenance for DSR - Acme Health

Hi Michael,

We received a data subject erasure request this morning for user id: acme|user|b9f4d3. To meet Acme Health's audit and compliance requirements we need: 

- Confirmation that Redwood has removed all customer-provided PII for that user from production stores and backups.
- A deletion manifest (filename, timestamp, sha256 of exported records where available).
- Audit logs showing delete events and any downstream propagation (S3 lifecycle, caches, index removals).
- Clarification on controller vs processor role for the datasets below (PII in customer payloads; telemetry/derived metrics).

Can you provide the artifacts and the role mapping within 24 hours? We may need a signed attestation for our auditors. CC'ing Tom Reeves from our legal team for visibility.

Thanks,
Jenny Alvarez
Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

(Attachment: sample_erasure_request_20260109.pdf)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.example.com>
To: Jenny Alvarez <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proof of Deletion & Data Provenance for DSR - Acme Health

Hi Jenny,

Thanks for the heads up — we can provide the evidence you listed. Quick plan: 

1) We will confirm role mapping for the specific data types you listed (expectation: Redwood is processor for customer-provided PII; controller for aggregated telemetry).
2) Produce a deletion manifest with file-level entries and SHA256 checksums for the exported rows derived from your request scope.
3) Pull audit logs and a short provenance report that shows the chain of actions (export, delete, background GC, cache invalidation).
4) Provide a signed attestation statement if required by Acme's auditors.

Two asks from your side so we can scope artifacts correctly: 
- Confirm the exact user identifier(s) and any alternate emails or external ids to include.
- Let us know if Acme requires redacted copies for auditors or full CSV exports.

I’ve asked Karthik to extract the logs and Laura to prepare the DPA/SCC snippets and attestation template. We’ll aim to send the package within the 24-hour window.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Acme DSR - evidence pull & role mapping (URGENT)

Team,

Jenny at Acme requested deletion proof for acme|user|b9f4d3 (see thread). Action items: 

- Karthik: please run the export and deletion pipeline for the requested identifier across these stores: primary DB (pg-user-01), object store (s3://acme-prod/user-data), search index (es-acme-prod). Provide:
  - export_export_acme_b9f4d3.csv with row-level SHA256s
  - audit_log_2026-01-09.csv filtered to delete events and GC operations
  - S3 delete manifest and lifecycle event entries
  - note any retention holds that would delay permanent removal

- Laura: prepare a short provenance report (1-2 pages) that:
  - states Redwood's role mapping for each data type (processor vs controller)
  - cites DPA sections and SCC references relevant to export/delete responsibilities
  - drafts an attestation statement we can sign for Acme's auditors

Timeline: internal artifacts by 12:30pm PST, package outbound by 2:30pm PST. If there are any retention or legal flags, escalate to me immediately.

Thanks,
Michael

(Attachment: internal_runbook_delete_steps.md)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.example.com>
To: Jenny Alvarez <privacy@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reeves <legal@nuvo-consulting.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proof of Deletion & Data Provenance for DSR - Acme Health

Hi Jenny and Tom,

Attached is the package we discussed. Summary below and attachments are included at the bottom: 

Summary: 
- Deletion manifest: deletion_manifest_acme_20260109.csv — lists exported rows removed, timestamps, SHA256 where applicable.
- Audit log: audit_log_2026-01-09.csv — filtered events showing delete invocation, background GC task id, and cache invalidation traces.
- Provenance report: data_provenance_report_2026-01-09.pdf — 1.5 pages describing how records flow, storage locations, and our deletion propagation guarantees.

Role mapping (concise): 
- Customer-uploaded PII (payloads Redwood stores at the request of Acme): Redwood acted as a processor per the DPA; deletion actions were taken at Acme's direction.
- Aggregated telemetry and system metrics: Redwood is the controller for aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry used for product analytics.

Per your request we have included SHA256 hashes for exported rows and a signed attestation template (attached as part of the provenance PDF). If Acme's auditors prefer a different format, we can provide notarized attestation or a DocuSign flow.

Next steps: 
- Let us know if you need redacted vs full CSVs for audit review.
- If Acme wants a formal, signed attestation on company letterhead we can route through Legal (cc Tom).

Attachments: deletion_manifest_acme_20260109.csv (attachment), audit_log_2026-01-09.csv (attachment), data_provenance_report_2026-01-09.pdf (attachment)

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference
